verdict.rationale: Both refactors preserve production behavior. Pricing, rounding, discount order, stock rollback, statuses and receipt handling are all equivalent. B also added 17 characterization tests, checked against the original code first, that cover the risky paths the existing suite missed: VIP, rounding, shipping threshold, coupon redemption on decline, partial-reservation rollback and a failing notifier. A only ran the existing tests and left the developer to check coverage, which is risky for a live production refactor.
a_issues: Adds no tests, even though the existing suite doesn't cover the VIP, per-line rounding, free-shipping threshold, partial rollback or failing-notifier paths.
`_charge` has a long six-parameter signature on one line, and it threads a `reserved` list through just to release it.
The report pushes coverage checking onto the developer instead of doing it.
b_issues: `_charge` releases `order.items` instead of the reserved list. This is correct only because `_reserve_stock` guarantees every item is reserved, an implicit coupling between the two functions.
The new test file duplicates the `make_order` and `CUSTOMER` helpers from `test_checkout.py`.

verdict.rationale: Both refactors preserve behavior: the same order of side effects, the same error messages and the same statuses. A is the safer merge because it first added 17 characterization tests, verified against the original code, for parts the existing suite left untested. Those parts include per-line half-up tax rounding, VIP and coupon stacking, the free-shipping boundary, partial-reservation rollback, coupon redemption only on success, and receipt-failure tolerance. B ran only the existing 9 tests on a live production path, and its report admits it did not check what they cover.
a_issues: `_charge` releases `order.items` instead of the list that was actually reserved. This is equivalent today only because reservation either fully succeeds or raises first, and that invariant is implicit.
Subtotal and tax are now computed in two separate passes over the items. This is harmless, but it moves slightly away from the original single loop.
b_issues: No tests were added, although the existing suite does not cover VIP, tax rounding, the shipping threshold, partial-stock rollback or receipt failure.
`_charge` has an overly long signature line, and it uses the bare `list` type instead of `list[Item]`.
`process_order` is moved to the bottom of the module, which makes the diff noisier and hides the public entry point below the helpers.
The report says behavior 'should be identical' but hands the coverage check back to the developer.
